chief_complaint: multiple bruises and healing lip cut after reported fall
hpi_details: 34F who is 10 weeks pregnant presents to the emergency department alone, leaving her husband in the waiting room, initially reporting she fell down stairs. She has a healing cut on her lip, multiple bruises of varying ages on her upper arms, and ulnar-side bruising on her forearm suggestive of defensive injuries. When interviewed privately and non-judgmentally, she discloses that her husband has been physically abusing her for the past year, which has escalated since she became pregnant. She reports being pushed and hit, but initially attributed her injuries to a fall due to fear.
ideas: believes her husband will retaliate if he finds out she disclosed the abuse
concerns: worried about the safety of her unborn baby and her two young children at home
expectations: wants her arm checked and hopes for confidential guidance on safety planning
pmh: G3P2, currently 10 weeks pregnant. No other significant past medical history.
social_hx: Married, living with husband and two children (ages 4 and 7). Non-smoker, no alcohol use.

boundaries_and_exceptions: The clinician must respect the patient's autonomy and readiness to change; leaving an abusive partner is highly dangerous, so do not pressure the patient into sudden decisions.

Mandatory reporting laws vary; while child abuse reporting is strictly mandatory, reporting adult domestic violence to law enforcement against a competent patient's wishes can sometimes increase their risk of harm. Local protocols in South Korea must be balanced with patient safety.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that victims of abuse will voluntarily disclose the violence without being asked directly and privately.
Believing that the physician's role is to confront the abuser or force the patient to leave the relationship immediately.
Failing to ask about the safety of other dependents in the home, such as young children.
Accepting an injury mechanism (like falling down stairs) that does not match the physical exam findings without further probing.
core_concepts: Intimate partner violence often escalates during pregnancy, making routine, private screening critical for all pregnant patients.
Injuries inconsistent with the stated mechanism (e.g., defensive ulnar bruises, multiple injuries in different stages of healing) should raise immediate suspicion for non-accidental trauma.
Patient safety is paramount; discussions must occur privately without the partner present to ensure safe disclosure and prevent immediate retaliation.
Management focuses on validation, comprehensive documentation, danger assessment (weapons, strangulation, threats to kill), and offering safety planning rather than forcing immediate departure.
dangerous_errors: Interviewing the patient or discussing suspicions of abuse with the partner present in the room.
Failing to screen for high-lethality indicators such as access to weapons, recent escalation, or prior strangulation.
Not asking about or ensuring the safety of the children in the home.
Discharging the patient without offering safety planning, shelter information (such as the 1366 hotline), or resources.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: multiple bruises and healing lip cut after reported fall

Key HPI features: 34F, 10 weeks pregnant, presents with injuries inconsistent with her story of falling down stairs. Displays defensive ulnar-side bruising on the forearm, bruises of varying ages on upper arms, and a healing lip cut.
Behavioral clues: Husband waits outside while she comes in alone; initial reluctance to disclose the true mechanism of injury due to fear.
Relevant background: Currently pregnant, which is a recognized high-risk period for the escalation of intimate partner violence.
management_principles: Ensure a completely private, non-judgmental environment for the interview and examination, away from the partner.
Perform a targeted lethality assessment, specifically screening for prior strangulation, access to weapons, and threats to kill.
Assess the safety of the children at home, as intimate partner violence often co-occurs with child abuse.
Develop a patient-centered safety plan and provide emergency resources, such as the Women's Emergency Hotline (1366) and local shelter information.
Obtain an X-ray of the forearm to rule out an underlying ulnar fracture and document all injuries objectively.

source_refs.title: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 518: Intimate Partner Violence
WHO guidelines for responding to intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women

reference_soap.assessment: Intimate partner violence with physical injuries (defensive forearm bruising, lip laceration) in a patient who is 10 weeks pregnant.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Stable. General: Anxious, avoiding eye contact initially. HEENT: Healing 1cm laceration on lower lip. MSK/Skin: Ecchymoses of varying ages on bilateral upper arms. Left forearm reveals significant ulnar-side bruising (defensive injury pattern). Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no palpable uterine contractions.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Ensure patient safety and maintain privacy; do not confront the husband. 2. Thoroughly document all injuries with a body map and photographs (with consent). 3. Assess immediate lethality risk and children's safety at home. 4. Order X-ray of the left forearm to rule out an ulnar fracture. 5. Provide safety planning and connect with resources, including the 1366 Women's Emergency Hotline. 6. Arrange close follow-up and prenatal care.
reference_soap.subjective: 34F, G3P2 at 10 weeks gestation, presents with multiple bruises and a healing lip laceration. Initially reported falling down stairs, but upon private questioning, disclosed that her husband has been physically abusing her for a year, with escalating violence since she became pregnant. She reports being pushed and hit. No abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding. Husband is in the waiting room.

learning_objectives: Recognize physical exam findings inconsistent with the reported mechanism of injury, such as defensive ulnar bruises and injuries in multiple stages of healing.
Demonstrate the ability to transition smoothly and empathetically to a private screening for intimate partner violence.
Conduct a comprehensive risk assessment for severe harm, including screening for weapons, strangulation, and the safety of children in the home.
Collaborate with the patient to formulate a safe discharge plan, providing appropriate resources like the 1366 hotline without violating her autonomy.

teaching.diagnosis: Intimate partner violence with physical injury in pregnancy

must_ask.say: Can you tell me exactly how you got those bruises on your forearm?
When was the first day of your last menstrual period?

must_ask.objective: Screening for abuse in a safe, normalized way
must_ask.say: Because it is so common, I ask all my patients: has anyone been hitting or hurting you at home?
Has he ever choked you or threatened you with a weapon?
Are your two children safe right now, and has he ever hurt them?
Do you have a safe place to go, and can I give you the 1366 shelter hotline information?

teaching.one_liner: A pregnant woman presenting with defensive injuries and bruises of varying ages who requires a safe, private environment to disclose escalating domestic abuse and receive safety planning.
red_flags: Injuries inconsistent with the history provided
Partner refusing to leave the room or answering questions for the patient

history.answer: I hurt my left arm after falling down the stairs, and I wanted to get it checked out.
Thank you for closing the door and speaking with me alone. It actually wasn't a fall... my husband hit me and pushed me.
It happened yesterday evening in our living room. My husband lost his temper and started hitting and shoving me.
He hit me with his fists and shoved me against the wall. Right now, my left forearm and my lower lip hurt the most.
No, he didn't choke me or strike my head. I never lost consciousness, felt dizzy, or had trouble swallowing.
The abuse started about a year ago, but it has gotten much worse and more frequent since I got pregnant. He hasn't used weapons or threatened my life yet.
My husband is sitting out in the waiting room right now. I am really afraid to go back home with him today.
We have two young kids at home, ages four and seven. He hasn't physically hurt them, but they hear the yelling and saw me crying.
Yes, he constantly checks my phone, controls all our household money, and tries to stop me from seeing my family.
No, he did not force me sexually yesterday, and this hasn't involved sexual violence.
No, nothing like that happened. I was completely alert and remember everything clearly.
I can barely sleep at night because I feel terrified and constantly on edge. I startle at the smallest noise.
No, I have never thought about ending my life or hurting myself. I just want to protect my children and my unborn baby.
I have never called the police or gone to a shelter before because I was too scared. My mother lives nearby, but I was ashamed to tell her.
I want an X-ray for my arm, and I really need private advice on how to keep myself and my children safe.
I am terrified that if he finds out I told you what really happened, he will become even more violent.
I am ten weeks pregnant right now. I am terribly worried about whether the stress and violence could hurt the baby.
No, he didn't hit my stomach, and I have not had any cramping, belly pain, or vaginal bleeding.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure or diabetes. I have had two healthy previous pregnancies.
I had two normal hospital deliveries with my older children, but no surgeries or other hospital stays.
I only take my daily prenatal vitamins. I do not take any other prescription or over-the-counter medicines.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or materials.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes.
I do not drink any alcohol, especially now that I am pregnant.
I am a stay-at-home mother, and I live with my husband and our two young children.
There is no family history of bleeding disorders or major chronic illnesses.
My last menstrual period was ten weeks ago, and my monthly cycles were always regular before this planned pregnancy.

exam.finding: Patient appears anxious, tearful, and avoids eye contact initially, but remains alert and cooperative.
Blood pressure is 118/74 mmHg, pulse 78 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert and oriented to person, place, and time, with clear speech and no cognitive impairment.
Sclerae are anicteric and conjunctivae are clear without petechiae, jaundice, or subconjunctival hemorrhage.
Healing 1-centimeter laceration on the left lower lip with mild swelling and tenderness; oral cavity is otherwise clear without dental trauma.
Multiple ecchymoses of varying ages on bilateral upper arms and prominent purplish bruising along the ulnar border of the left forearm.
Localized tenderness and soft tissue edema over the left distal ulna without gross deformity; wrist and elbow range of motion is intact.
Chest wall is non-tender to palpation with symmetric expansion and no rib contusions or crepitus.
Abdomen is soft, non-distended, and non-tender throughout with no guarding, rebound tenderness, or palpable uterine contractions.
